title: Sliding-Window Streaming VLMs: Full Evaluation — Qwen3.8-27B vs Muse Glimmer 30B
summary: Qwen3.8-27B and Muse Glimmer 30B run as causal online assistants (an 8-frame sliding window plus a memory they write themselves, replayed in media time) on the Wearable AI validation split (2,056 sessions) and on Ego-MC-Bench (39 videos) under the Ego-MC-Bench paper's own evaluation protocol and official evaluator, so the Ego-MC numbers are directly comparable to the paper. An isolated latency study compares both models with and without reasoning.

title: Human–Device Simulation — a rigged human operating a microwave and a desktop printer (3D render + MuJoCo contact)
summary: Reproducible 3D pipeline: a clothed MPFB human with IK-driven hands operates a CC BY 4.0 microwave model and a generic desktop printer in Blender; each device's key (microwave START, printer OK) is driven by MuJoCo contact against a kinematic fingertip proxy with a negative control; door, knob, bowl, paper tray and paper stack use labelled assisted grasps; the turntable, interior light, display and printed sheet are labelled motor or illustrative effects. Two recorded runs (microwave 51 s, printer 35 s) rendered from external, first-person and hand-detail cameras (preview quality). 2026-10-11: three procedural devices built from reference videos (Samsung-style microwave with 21 contact keys, Breville-style espresso machine, Frigidaire-style induction range with a touch panel), four tasks each, all rendered from three cameras; the old microwave runs stay on the page.
